newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa budget GDP forecast conservative - Manuel.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa budget GDP forecast conservative - Manuel.

text.p: South African Finance Minister Trevor Manuel said on Thursday that the budget assumption of growth in gross domestic product (GDP) of 2.5 percent in 1997 was conservative but not unduly pessimistic.
Noting that a number of analysts, together with the Reserve Bank, were painting a more upbeat picture of growth this year, Manuel told parliament's finance committee:
"When we did this we were at the bullish end of the spectrum. The consensus then was for two percent, if you are lucky, and that was just recently...

"I don't think it's over-pessimistic, but I would rather, in the circumstance, have over-performance than to set our sights so high and underperform. It's a judgement call and I don't think we are too far off, because in general terms it is a year of consolidation."
In the last month or so views on growth have been revised up, encouraged by data showing an uptick in fourth quarter 1996 output which lifted real GDP growth last year to 3.1 percent.
Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals told Reuters earlier this month that the economy could again expand by close to three percent in 1997.
"It's nice to see the Governor is a bit more bullish than we are," Manuel said.
